Anthropic revenue jumps to US$16.8 billion in quarter before IPO The Business Times

Anthropic revenue jumps to US$16.8 billion in Q3 before IPO The Straits Times
reactions: [Hacker News] Previously: "Anthropic is now pacing to generate more than $100 billion in annual revenue, up 50% from just two months ago, the New York Times reported Friday." https://www.axios.com/2026/09/18/anthropic-100-billion-reven... So then, by this magic revenue number ARR (multiply our best month by 12), we multiply this best quarter by 4 and get $87.52?

[Hacker News] They are in serious trouble. The only solid outcome for the powers that be is that VC is allowed to cash out and re-invest it to ensure America stays ahead. Whatever happens to employee shares - who cares. The gap between China and USA is closing. Im not talking LLMs. Im talking purely about innovation - USA may be technically more creative but China are great a) copying b) latching on and coming

[Hacker News] I'm sure this has been discussed elsewhere, but I was recently befuddled at just how insanely the OpenRouter rankings graph has grown this year. Look at this shit: https://openrouter.ai/rankings Am I to understand the weekly pace has gone from 3.2T tokens to 181T tokens since last October? AI will have many problems but it seems profitability (maybe) ain't one.
[Hacker News] There's a well established phenomena called managed earnings.

[Hacker News] The biggest risk for Anthropic is that they have committed to a certain expenditure level. If they are not yet profitable at that time or if they can not raise more they could get into serious trouble.
[Hacker News] That at least explains some of the more panicky blog posts they have been producing.
[Hacker News] Makes you wonder how much of q3 revenue growth was early on. And what’s the current MoM growth.
[Hacker News] No sweat. Those bonds are going to be converted into equity and dumped on retail investors when they go public.
